Examples

Every circuit in the oracle corpus — 78 decks — plus 29 pic schematics: the netlist, and what Dune computes for it. Each result was produced by Dune's WebAssembly build (dune-sim 0.3.6) when this page was generated; the same decks are checked point by point against ngspice-47 in CI. Transient charts are re-run with the max internal step capped at 1/600 of the window, so the curves carry enough timepoints to draw smoothly — the deck shown, on its own grid, is what CI compares.

Charts show at most 6 vectors (the deck's own .plot/.print choice when it has one), decimated to min/max per pixel column; complex plots show magnitude. Known-marginal circuits (corpus/XFAIL) and failures are shown as they are.

Figures (pic) 29

Schematics in rpic's pic language (corpus/pic/): the source, the figure Dune renders from it, the netlist its extractor derives, and the simulation of that netlist. corpus/pic/spice.pic is the prelude itself, not a figure.

basic/acdiode.cir drawn: a 1 mA bias (with a 1 mA AC part) into a diode shunted by 100k; .ac sees the diode's small-signal model at that bias, rd = n Vt / Id = 25.9 ohm plus RS, against CJ + Cd

corpus/pic/acdiode.pic.ac#
acdiode.pic
.PS
# basic/acdiode.cir drawn: a 1 mA bias (with a 1 mA AC part) into a
# diode shunted by 100k; .ac sees the diode's small-signal model at
# that bias, rd = n Vt / Id = 25.9 ohm plus RS, against CJ + Cd.
# Card order kept; deck node 1 Va.
spice = 1
Va: (1.3,1.6)

Ibias: isource((0.3,0), (0.3,1.6), dc 1m ac 1m)
D1: diode((1.3,1.6), (1.3,0), dmod)
Rsh: resistor((2.3,1.6), (2.3,0), 100k)

line from Ibias.N to Rsh.P
line from Ibias.P to Rsh.N
dot at Va; dot at D1.N
ground((0.8,0))
.model dmod d(is=1e-14 rs=10 cjo=5p tt=10n vj=0.8 m=0.4)
.ac oct 8 1k 100meg
.PE
the figure — rendered by Dune's rpic
dune pic acdiode.pic
* netlist extracted by dune-pic
Ibias 0 Va dc 1m ac 1m
D1 Va 0 dmod
Rsh Va 0 100k
.model dmod d(is=1e-14 rs=10 cjo=5p tt=10n vj=0.8 m=0.4)
.ac oct 8 1k 100meg
.end

basic/acrlc.cir drawn: a 2 V / 45 degree drive into a pair of 10u coils coupled by k = 0.3; the secondary rings a series 5 ohm / 253.3p branch (f0 = 3.16 MHz) and a VCVS (x2) buffers the secondary into RE. Card order kept; deck nodes 1 In, 2 Pri, 3 Sec, 4 Vc, 5 Vout

.PS
# basic/acrlc.cir drawn: a 2 V / 45 degree drive into a pair of 10u
# coils coupled by k = 0.3; the secondary rings a series 5 ohm /
# 253.3p branch (f0 = 3.16 MHz) and a VCVS (x2) buffers the secondary
# into RE. Card order kept; deck nodes 1 In, 2 Pri, 3 Sec, 4 Vc,
# 5 Vout.

In:   (0.3,2)
Pri:  (1.4,2)
Sec:  (2.4,2)
Vc:   (3.5,2)
Vout: (5.1,2)

Vin: acsource((0.3,2), (0.3,0), ac 2 45)
RS: resistor((0.3,2), (1.4,2), 50)
L1: inductor((1.4,2), (1.4,0), 10u)
L2: inductor((2.4,2), (2.4,0), 10u)

line from Sec to (2.4,2.6) then to (4.3,2.6) then to (4.3,1.2) then to E1.Cp
line from E1.Cn to (4.3,0.8) then to (4.3,0)
line from E1.P to RE.P
line from Vin.N to RE.N
dot at Sec

Series RLC band-pass, output across R1

corpus/pic/bandpass.pic.ac#
bandpass.pic
.PS
# Series RLC band-pass, output across R1:
# H = R/(R + j w L + 1/(j w C)); f0 = 1/(2 pi sqrt(L1 C1)) = 15.9 kHz,
# |H(f0)| = 1, bandwidth R1/(2 pi L1) = 7.96 kHz (Q = 2).
spice = 1
Vin: (0,1.5); Vout: (3,1.5)
V1: vsource(Vin, (0,0), AC 1)
L1: inductor(Vin, (1.5,1.5), 1m)
C1: capacitor(L1.N, Vout, 100n)
R1: resistor(Vout, (3,0), 50)
line from V1.N to R1.N
ground((1.5,0))
dot at Vout
"out" above at Vout + (0,0.05)
.ac dec 20 1k 1meg
.PE
the figure — rendered by Dune's rpic
dune pic bandpass.pic
* netlist extracted by dune-pic
V1 Vin 0 AC 1
L1 Vin n1 1m
C1 n1 Vout 100n
R1 Vout 0 50
.ac dec 20 1k 1meg
.end

Current-controlled sources read the current through V0, a 0 V ammeter in series with R1: i(v0) = 2 V / 1k = 2 mA. The CCCS

corpus/pic/ccprobe.pic.op#
ccprobe.pic
.PS
# Current-controlled sources read the current through V0, a 0 V
# ammeter in series with R1: i(v0) = 2 V / 1k = 2 mA. The CCCS
# (gain 3) pulls 6 mA out of Va through itself, so v(va) = -6 V across
# R2; the CCVS (500 ohm transresistance) sets v(vb) = 1 V across R3.
spice = 1
In: (0.3,2)
Vs: (1.5,2)
Va: (3.6,2)
Vb: (5.6,2)

V1: vsource((0.3,2), (0.3,0), DC 2)
R1: resistor((0.3,2), (1.5,2), 1k)
V0: vsource((1.5,2), (1.5,0), DC 0)
F1: cccs((2.8,2), (2.8,0), V0 3)
R2: resistor((3.6,2), (3.6,0), 1k)
H1: ccvs((4.8,2), (4.8,0), V0 500)
R3: resistor((5.6,2), (5.6,0), 1k)

line from F1.P to R2.P
line from H1.P to R3.P
line from V1.N to R3.N
dot at V0.N; dot at F1.N; dot at R2.N; dot at H1.N
ground(V1.N)
.op
.PE
the figure — rendered by Dune's rpic

* netlist extracted by dune-pic
V1 In 0 DC 2
R1 In Vs 1k
V0 Vs 0 DC 0
F1 Va 0 V0 3
R2 Va 0 1k
H1 Vb 0 V0 500
R3 Vb 0 1k
.op
.end

CMOS inverter (MOS1) driving 1 pF: a 0 -> 5 V input pulse flips the output rail to rail; no static current in either state

corpus/pic/cmosinv.pic.tran#
cmosinv.pic
.PS
# CMOS inverter (MOS1) driving 1 pF: a 0 -> 5 V input pulse flips the
# output rail to rail; no static current in either state.
spice = 1
M2: pmos((2,2.1), PMOD W=8u L=1u, "T₂")
M1: nmos((2,0.9), NMOD W=4u L=1u, "T₁")
Vin:  (1.2,1.5)
Vout: (M1.D.x,1.5)
Vdd:  (M2.S.x,2.7)

V1: vsource((0.3,1.5), (0.3,0), PULSE(0 5 5n 1n 1n 20n 50n), "G₁")
V2: vsource((6.2,2.7), (6.2,0), DC 5, "VDD")
C1: capacitor((4.2,1.5), (4.2,0), 1p)
line from M2.D to M1.D
line from M1.G to (Vin.x,M1.G.y) then to (Vin.x,M2.G.y) then to M2.G
line from V1.P to Vin
line from Vout to C1.P
line from M2.S to Vdd then to V2.P
line from M1.S to (M1.S.x,0)
line from V1.N to V2.N
dot at Vin; dot at Vout; dot at C1.P; dot at (M1.S.x,0); dot at C1.N
"in" above at (0.75,1.55)
line from C1.P to (4.8,1.5); circle rad 0.04 at (4.84,1.5)
"out" above at (4.84,1.55)
ground((1.2,0))
.model NMOD NMOS(LEVEL=1 VTO=0.7 KP=110u LAMBDA=0.04)
.model PMOD PMOS(LEVEL=1 VTO=-0.7 KP=50u LAMBDA=0.05)
.tran 0.1n 60n
.PE
the figure — rendered by Dune's rpic

Vout: (4.4,2)

V2: vsource((2.9,2), (2.9,0), dc 0)
R1: resistor((0.3,2), (1.6,2), 1k)
R2: resistor((2.9,2), (1.6,2), 2k)
R3: resistor((1.6,2), (1.6,0), 1k)
E1: vcvs((4.4,2), (4.4,0), (3.9,1.2), (3.9,0.8), -1.5)
R4: resistor((5.6,2), (5.6,0), 1k)

line from Vx to (1.6,2.6) then to (3.6,2.6) then to (3.6,1.2) then to E1.Cp
line from E1.Cn to (3.6,0.8) then to (3.6,0)
line from E1.P to R4.P
line from V1.N to R4.N
dot at Vx; dot at R3.N; dot at V2.N; dot at (3.6,0); dot at E1.N
ground((0.95,0))
.dc v1 0 1 0.25 v2 0 2 0.5
.PE

Berkeley's diffpair.cir drawn: an emitter-coupled pair Q1/Q2 with 10k collector loads, its tail current set by the Q3/Q4 mirror and Rbias (~0.56 mA). Elements are in the deck's card order, so the figure's netlist is the deck's with named nodes (1 In, 2 B1, 3 B2, 4 Vc1, 5 Vc2, 6 Tail, 7 Bias, 8 Vp, 9 Vn) and simulates identically

corpus/pic/diffpair.pic.tran#
diffpair.pic
.PS
# Berkeley's diffpair.cir drawn: an emitter-coupled pair Q1/Q2 with
# 10k collector loads, its tail current set by the Q3/Q4 mirror and
# Rbias (~0.56 mA). Elements are in the deck's card order, so the
# figure's netlist is the deck's with named nodes (1 In, 2 B1, 3 B2,
# 4 Vc1, 5 Vc2, 6 Tail, 7 Bias, 8 Vp, 9 Vn) and simulates identically.
spice = 1
Vin: vsource((0.3,2.5), (0.3,1.7), sin(0 0.1 5meg) ac 1, "G₁")
Vcc: vsource((6.2,4), (6.2,3.2), 12, "VCC")
Vee: vsource((6.2,0.3), (6.2,1.1), -12, "VEE")
Q1: npn((2.9,2.5), qnl, "T₁")
Q2: npn((5.2,2.5), qnl, "T₂")
RS1: resistor((1.5,2.5), Q1.B, 1k)
RS2: resistor(Q2.B, (3.9,2.5), 1k)
RC1: resistor(Q1.C, (Q1.C.x,4), 10k)
RC2: resistor(Q2.C, (Q2.C.x,4), 10k)
Q3: npn((4.3,1), qnl, "T₃")
Q4: npn((2.6,1), qnl, "T₄")
Rbias: resistor((1.2,1.42), (1.2,2.3), 20k)

In:   (0.3,2.5)
B1:   Q1.B
B2:   Q2.B
Vc1:  Q1.C
Vc2:  Q2.C
Tail: (Q3.C.x,1.7)
Bias: (1.95,1.42)
Vp:   (6.2,4)
Vn:   (6.2,0.3)

# input; the bias riser crosses it without a dot (no connection)
line from Vin.P to RS1.P
line from Rbias.N to (1.2,4) then to Vcc.P
# emitter-coupled tail and its current source
line from Q1.E to (Q1.E.x,1.7) then to (Q2.E.x,1.7) then to Q2.E
line from Q3.C to Tail
# mirror: Q4 diode-connected, its base/collector node drives Q3
line from Q3.B to (3.45,1) then to (3.45,1.42) then to Rbias.P
line from Q4.B to (1.95,1) then to Bias
line from Q4.E to (Q4.E.x,0.3) then to Vee.P
line from Q3.E to (Q3.E.x,0.3)
line from Vee.N to (6.6,1.1)
dot at Tail; dot at Q4.C; dot at Bias; dot at (Q3.E.x,0.3)
dot at RC1.N; dot at RC2.N
ground(Vin.N); ground(RS2.N); ground(Vcc.N); ground((6.6,1.1))

regress/mos3_inv.cir drawn: two level-3 CMOS inverters in cascade

corpus/pic/mos3_inv.pic.ac.op.tran#
mos3_inv.pic
.PS
# regress/mos3_inv.cir drawn: two level-3 CMOS inverters in cascade
# (T₁/T₂ drive T₃/T₄, 50f and 100f loads) and, on the right, a
# self-biased level-3 amplifier T₅ — 200k drain-to-gate feedback,
# 500 ohm source degeneration with the bulk on ground (a four-terminal
# MOS), 10k load. Card order kept; deck nodes 1 Vp, 2 In, 3 Out1,
# 4 Out2, 5 Ain, 6 Vg, 7 Vd, 8 Vs.
spice = 1
maxpswid = 12
Vp:   (11.2,3.1)
In:   (1.2,1.5)
Out1: (2.16,1.5)
Out2: (4.56,1.5)
Ain:  (6.8,1.2)
Vg:   (7.8,1.2)
Vd:   (8.96,2)
Vs:   (8.96,0.84)

Vdd: vsource((11.2,3.1), (11.2,0), dc 3.3, "VDD")
Vin: vsource((0.3,1.5), (0.3,0), dc 0 pulse(0 3.3 2n 1n 1n 8n 20n), "G₁")
MN1: nmos((2,0.9), n3 l=1u w=4u ad=8p as=8p pd=12u ps=12u, "T₁")
MP1: pmos((2,2.1), p3 l=1u w=10u ad=20p as=20p pd=24u ps=24u, "T₂")
C3: capacitor((3.2,1.5), (3.2,0), 50f)
MN2: nmos((4.4,0.9), n3 l=1u w=4u ad=8p as=8p pd=12u ps=12u, "T₃")
MP2: pmos((4.4,2.1), p3 l=1u w=10u ad=20p as=20p pd=24u ps=24u, "T₄")
C4: capacitor((5.6,1.5), (5.6,0), 100f)
Vac: vsource((6.8,1.2), (6.8,0), dc 0 ac 1, "G₂")
Cin: capacitor((6.8,1.2), (7.8,1.2), 10p)
RF: resistor((8.96,2), (7.8,2), 200k)
MN3: nmos4((8.8,1.2), n3 l=2u w=20u ad=40p as=40p pd=44u ps=44u, "T₅")
RS3: resistor((8.96,0.84), (8.96,0), 500)
RL: resistor((8.96,3.1), (8.96,2), 10k)
C7: capacitor((10.3,2), (10.3,0), 0.2p)

# the two inverters
line from Vin.P to In
line from MN1.G to (1.2,0.9) then to (1.2,2.1) then to MP1.G
line from MP1.D to MN1.D
line from Out1 to C3.P then to (3.6,1.5)
line from MN2.G to (3.6,0.9) then to (3.6,2.1) then to MP2.G
line from MP2.D to MN2.D
line from Out2 to C4.P
line from MN1.S to (2.16,0)
line from MN2.S to (4.56,0)
# the amplifier
line from Cin.N to MN3.G
line from RF.N to Vg
line from MN3.D to Vd then to C7.P
line from MN3.B to (9.4,1.2) then to (9.4,0)
# rails
line from MP1.S to (2.16,3.1) then to Vp
line from MP2.S to (4.56,3.1)
line from Vin.N to Vdd.N
dot at In; dot at Out1; dot at C3.P; dot at (3.6,1.5); dot at Out2
dot at Vg; dot at Vd
dot at (4.56,3.1); dot at RL.P
dot at (2.16,0); dot at C3.N; dot at (4.56,0); dot at C4.N; dot at Vac.N
dot at RS3.N; dot at (9.4,0); dot at C7.N
ground((0.75,0))
.model n3 nmos level=3 vto=0.6 nsub=4e16 tox=1.5e-8 xj=0.15u ld=0.05u u0=450
+ theta=0.06 eta=0.2 delta=0.6 vmax=1.6e5 kappa=0.4 nfs=6e11 rsh=15
+ cj=4e-4 mj=0.45 cjsw=3e-10 mjsw=0.3 cgso=2e-10 cgdo=2e-10 cgbo=1e-10
.model p3 pmos level=3 vto=-0.7 nsub=3e16 tox=1.5e-8 xj=0.2u ld=0.06u u0=180
+ theta=0.05 eta=0.15 delta=0.5 kappa=0.6 nfs=4e11 rsh=25
+ cj=5e-4 mj=0.5 cjsw=3.5e-10 mjsw=0.33 cgso=2.5e-10 cgdo=2.5e-10 cgbo=1e-10
.ac dec 10 10k 10g
.op
.tran 0.1n 40n
.PE

Vm:   (1.8,1.175)

"out" ljust at (4.4,1)

line from V1.N to (X1.Inp.x,0)

opamp_ideal.sub — pulled in by .include
* opamp_ideal.sub: a minimal op-amp macromodel for the dune-pic figures.
* A single-pole-free gain block with 741-datasheet typicals:
* open-loop gain 200k, input resistance 2 Meg, output resistance 75.
* (Not a 741 model: no pole, no slew, no output limiting.)
* Pins in the order the prelude's opamp() emits them (D-0020):
* non-inverting input, inverting input, output.
.subckt opamp_ideal inp inm out
rin inp inm 2meg
e1 int 0 inp inm 200k
rout int out 75
.ends opamp_ideal

Berkeley's rca3040.cir drawn: the RCA CA3040 wideband amplifier

corpus/pic/rca3040.pic.ac.dc.tran#
rca3040.pic
.PS
# Berkeley's rca3040.cir drawn: the RCA CA3040 wideband amplifier.
# Emitter followers T₁/T₂ drive the pair T₃/T₄, cascoded by T₅/T₆
# (their bases held by the diode string T₇/T₈ under R7); T₉ sinks the
# tail current set by R4/R5/R3, and T₁₀/T₁₁ buffer the two collector
# loads. Elements are in the deck's card order (pins are coordinates,
# so no transistor is referenced before its card), and the figure's
# netlist is the deck's with named nodes (1 In, 2 Vp, 3 Vn, 5 Ba,
# 6 Bb, 7 Tail, 8 Bias, 9 Vt, 10 Ca, 11 Cb, 12 Vcas, 13 Vd, 14 Oa,
# 15 Ob, 16 Out, 17 Outb, 30 B1, 31 B2). Two wires cross without a dot
# (no connection): the cascode bias into T₆ and T₂'s emitter into T₄,
# each over the T₃–T₅ / T₄–T₆ link. The deck's 3-node Q cards keep
# the substrate (CCS) on ground, so the plain npn symbol is used.
spice = 1
maxpswid = 12
In:   (0.2,4.4)
B1:   (1.52,4.4)
B2:   (8.92,4.4)
Vp:   (10.6,8.4)
Vn:   (10.6,0)
Ba:   (2.16,3.2)
Bb:   (9.56,3.85)
Tail: (6.16,2.3)
Bias: (4.4,1.6)
Vt:   (6.16,1.18)
Ca:   (4.76,3.8)
Cb:   (7.56,4.1)
Vcas: (3.4,7)
Vd:   (3.4,5.9)
Oa:   (4.76,6.6)
Ob:   (7.56,6.6)
Out:  (8.56,6.18)
Outb: (5.76,6.18)

.ac dec 10 1 10ghz
.dc vin -0.25 0.25 0.005
.tran 2.0ns 200ns
Vin: vsource((0.2,4.4), (0.2,3.2), sin(0 0.1 50meg 0.5ns) ac 1, "G₁")
Vcc: vsource((10.6,8.4), (10.6,7.2), 15.0, "VCC")
Vee: vsource((10.6,0), (10.6,1), -15.0, "VEE")
RS1: resistor((1.52,4.4), (0.2,4.4), 1k)
RS2: resistor((8.92,4.4), (7.95,4.4), 1k)
R1: resistor((2.16,3.2), (2.16,0), 4.8k)
R2: resistor((9.56,3.85), (9.56,0), 4.8k)
R3: resistor((6.16,1.18), (6.16,0), 811)
R4: resistor((4.4,1.6), (4.4,0), 2.17k)
R5: resistor((3.6,1.6), (3.6,0.6), 820)
R6: resistor((4.76,8.4), (4.76,6.6), 1.32k)
R7: resistor((3.4,8.4), (3.4,7), 4.5k)
R8: resistor((7.56,8.4), (7.56,6.6), 1.32k)
R9: resistor((8.56,6.18), (8.56,5.3), 5.25k)
R10: resistor((5.76,6.18), (5.76,5.3), 5.25k)
Q1: npn((2,4.4), qnl, "T₁")
Q2: npn((9.4,4.4), qnl, "T₂")
Q3: npn((4.6,3.2), qnl, "T₃")
Q4: npn((7.4,3.2), qnl, "T₄")
Q5: npn((4.6,4.8), qnl, "T₅")
Q6: npn((7.4,4.8), qnl, "T₆")
Q7: npn((3.24,6.4), qnl, "T₇")
Q8: npn((3.24,5.4), qnl, "T₈")
Q9: npn((6,1.6), qnl, "T₉")
Q10: npn((8.4,6.6), qnl, "T₁₀")
Q11: npn((5.6,6.6), qnl, "T₁₁")

# supply rails
line from Q1.C to (2.16,8.4) then to Vcc.P
line from Q11.C to (5.76,8.4)
line from Q10.C to (8.56,8.4)
line from Q2.C to (9.56,8.4)
line from R1.N to Vee.P
line from Vee.N to (11,1)
# input followers into the pair
line from Q1.E to Ba then to Q3.B
line from Q2.E to Bb then to (6.75,3.85) then to (6.75,3.2) then to Q4.B
# pair, cascode, tail
line from Q3.C to Q5.E
line from Q4.C to Q6.E
line from Q3.E to (4.76,2.3) then to (7.56,2.3) then to Q4.E
line from Q9.C to Tail
line from Q9.B to (3.6,1.6)
# cascode bias: the T₇/T₈ diode string
line from Q7.C to Vcas
line from Q7.B to (2.76,7) then to Vcas then to (4,7) then to (4,4.1) \
  then to (6.6,4.1) then to (6.6,4.8) then to Q6.B
line from (4,4.8) to Q5.B
line from Q7.E to Q8.C
line from Q8.B to (2.76,5.9) then to Vd
# collector loads into the output followers
line from Oa to Q5.C
line from Oa to Q11.B
line from Ob to Q6.C
line from Ob to Q10.B
dot at (3.4,8.4); dot at (4.76,8.4); dot at (5.76,8.4); dot at (7.56,8.4)
dot at (8.56,8.4); dot at (9.56,8.4)
dot at (4.4,0); dot at (6.16,0); dot at (9.56,0)
dot at Ba; dot at Bb; dot at Tail; dot at Bias; dot at Vcas; dot at Vd
dot at (4,4.8); dot at Oa; dot at Ob
ground(Vin.N); ground(RS2.N); ground(R5.N); ground(Q8.E)
ground(R9.N); ground(R10.N); ground(Vcc.N); ground((11,1))
.model qnl npn bf=80 rb=100 ccs=2pf tf=0.3ns tr=6ns cje=3pf
+ cjc=2pf va 50
.PE

AC decade grid over a non-whole-decade span lands on FSTOP (ngspice)

corpus/regress/acdec.cir.ac#
acdec.cir
AC decade grid over a non-whole-decade span lands on FSTOP (ngspice)
* Regression: ngspice-47 (acan.c) recomputes the decade step as
* exp(ln(stop/start)/floor(log10(stop/start)*n)) whenever the span
* exceeds one decade, so the sweep ends exactly at FSTOP; the 3f5's
* 10^(1/n) agrees only on whole-decade spans. 10meg->2g spans 2.30
* decades: the grids differ at every point past the first without
* the ngspice form. Under one decade (and stop==start) the 3f5 step
* survives in both programs.
vin 1 0 dc 0 ac 1
r1 1 2 1k
c1 2 0 15.9p
r2 2 3 10k
l1 3 0 1u
.ac dec 10 10meg 2g
.end
AC Analysismagnitudelog f
v(2)v(3)(+3 more vectors)

BSIM1 transient overlap caps use drawn W and effective L (b1ld.c)

corpus/regress/b1overlap.cir.tran#
b1overlap.cir
BSIM1 transient overlap caps use drawn W and effective L (b1ld.c)
* Regression: the transient load builds the gate overlap caps from the
* DRAWN width (gs/gd) and the EFFECTIVE length (gb), per b1ld.c, while
* b1temp.c's per-instance values (effective W, drawn L) feed only the
* AC load. Dune once used the b1temp.c values in both places. Here the
* gate pulse (device always cut off) couples through Cgdo onto a
* floating 1 fF drain node, and the stored plateau voltage measures
* the overlap cap directly: drawn vs effective W differs by ~24%.
m1 2 1 0 0 nmos l=2u w=2u ad=0.1p as=0.1p

One-BJT common-emitter amplifier: intermodulation in .disto

corpus/regress/bjtdisto2.cir.disto#
bjtdisto2.cir
One-BJT common-emitter amplifier: intermodulation in .disto
* Coverage: every Gummel-Poon nonlinearity bjtdset.c expands - the
* junction and leakage currents (ISE/ISC), Early (VAF/VAR), roll-off
* (IKF/IKR, the qb square root), the bias-dependent base resistance
* with IRB (the tan(z) chain and its power-series inversion), the
* transit time with XTF/VTF/ITF, excess phase (PTF: the delayed-vbe
* rotation of every kernel), the B-C capacitance split by XCJC (qbx
* on the external base) and the substrate capacitance - through the
* IM products f1+f2, f1-f2, 2f1-f2 against ngspice-47.
* Supply, input and substrate are Norton equivalents (a current
* source across a resistor) so every compared vector is a node
* voltage: the residual vs the golden is a uniform ~5e-5 relative
* (ngspice's physical constants move vt by 2.8e-5, and the
* coefficients go as Ic/vt^n), which a branch current crossing zero
* in one component would turn into a pointwise failure of the ruler.
icc 0 5 12
rcc 5 0 1
iin 0 1 0 distof1 2.5u distof2 2.5u
rs 1 0 1k
cin 1 3 10u
rb1 5 3 82k
rb2 3 0 15k
rc 5 4 4.7k
re 6 0 1k
ce 6 0 100u
q1 4 3 6 7 qmod
isub 7 0 2
rsub 7 0 1
.model qmod npn is=1e-15 bf=150 nf=1.01 vaf=60 ikf=20m ise=2e-14 ne=1.6
+ br=3 nr=1.02 var=20 ikr=5m isc=1e-14 nc=1.8
+ rb=150 irb=0.2m rbm=30 re=2 rc=15
+ cje=2p vje=0.8 mje=0.35 tf=0.4n xtf=2 vtf=4 itf=30m ptf=25
+ cjc=1.5p vjc=0.6 mjc=0.4 xcjc=0.6 tr=5n cjs=1p vjs=0.7 mjs=0.4
.disto dec 10 1e3 1e9 0.9
.end

Current-controlled switch: W cards keyed by a separate control loop

corpus/regress/csw_rly.cir.dc.tran#
csw_rly.cir
Current-controlled switch: W cards keyed by a separate control loop
* Coverage: no corpus deck has a W card. vi drives 0 -> 5 mA -> 0 through
* the sense source vsense in its own loop; w1 (IT=2.4m, IH=0.9m: closes
* above 3.3 mA, opens below 1.5 mA) charges c3 through RON and lets it
* bleed through rl1 when open, like a relay contact. w5 watches the
* mirrored loop (vsense2 carries 5 mA - i(vsense)), so the rising .dc
* also falls through a window. w2/w3 share a model whose window
* (-0.6m..5.4m) contains the whole control range: CSWload (ngspice)
* holds the state of the last *accepted* point (state1) inside the
* window, which is zero in the operating point, so w2 opens despite its
* ON hint (the 3f5 and SWload keep it closed). w4 has a negative IH.
vi 10 0 dc 0 pwl(0 0 1m 5 2m 0)
rctl 10 11 1k
vsense 11 0 dc 0
vo 12 0 dc 5
e1 13 12 10 0 -1
rctl2 13 14 1k
vsense2 14 0 dc 0
vdd 2 0 dc 10
w1 2 3 vsense wmod
rl1 3 0 1k
c3 3 0 100n
w2 2 4 vsense wwin on
rl2 4 0 1k
w3 2 5 vsense wwin off
rl3 5 0 1k
w4 2 6 vsense wneg
rl4 6 0 1k
w5 2 7 vsense2 wmod
rl5 7 0 1k
.model wmod csw it=2.4m ih=0.9m ron=10 roff=1e6
.model wwin csw it=2.4m ih=3m ron=100 roff=1e5
.model wneg csw it=2.4m ih=-0.7m ron=50 roff=2e5
.dc vi 0 5 0.2
.tran 20u 2m
.end

Diode noise: RS thermal, junction shot and flicker in .noise

corpus/regress/dionoise2.cir.noise#
dionoise2.cir
Diode noise: RS thermal, junction shot and flicker in .noise
* Coverage: dionoise.c in its ngspice-47 form - the RS thermal source
* between the anode and its internal node, shot noise of the junction
* current, KF*|Id|^AF/f flicker, and the three sidewall vectors
* (_rsw/_idsw/_1overfsw) ngspice always names, zero without RSW. d2
* has area 2 (RS conductance and current both scale) and sits in the
* signal path to the output, so its generators see a nontrivial
* transfer; d1 shunts the input node. TT and CJO shape the band.

rin 1 2 10k
ib 0 2 dc 200u
d1 2 0 dn
d2 2 3 dn 2
rl 3 0 2k
.model dn d is=1e-14 rs=25 n=1.2 tt=5n cjo=2p kf=1e-14 af=1.2
.noise v(3) vin dec 10 1 1g 1
.end

ltrafit.cir
LTRA recursive convolution (ltrafit): RLC and RC lines, 300 ns history
* Gate of Dune's opt-in recursive mode (issue #8): ngspice-47 runs the
* faithful coefficient walk (it ignores the unknown option), Dune the
* exponential-sum recursion. Mismatched loads keep both lines
* reflecting for the whole run, the load capacitors make the
* integration method matter (tests/ltra_fit.rs reruns it under
* method=trbdf2); 3000+ accepted points exercise the snapshot
* pruning; R/2L*TSTOP = 3.3 reaches the h1' tail.

rs 1 2 10
o1 2 0 3 0 rlcline
rl 3 0 100
cl 3 0 2pF
rs2 1 4 10
o2 4 0 5 0 rcline
rl2 5 0 100
cl2 5 0 2pF
.model rlcline ltra r=0.2 l=9.13e-9 c=3.65e-12 len=24
.model rcline ltra r=0.2 l=0 c=3.65e-12 len=24
.options ltrafit
.tran 0.1ns 300ns
.end

.end

corpus/regress/mos2disto.cir.disto#
mos2disto.cir
MOS2 common-source stage: intermodulation in .disto
* Coverage: mos2dset.c's Dderivs chain through the Grove-Frohman
* current - narrow-channel factor (DELTA), the XJ short-channel
* correction of gamma, and the NSUB channel-length modulation from
* XD (LAMBDA=0) - plus the shared MOS load, through f1+f2, f1-f2 and
* 2f1-f2. GAMMA=0 keeps
* the deck off the two places where mos2dset.c reads storage it never
* wrote (d_dumarg with GAMMA>0, d_xlamda with LAMBDA>0 or no NSUB);
* see the rustdoc of Mos2I::disto_coeffs.
vdd 5 0 5
vin 1 0 0 distof1 0.02 distof2 0.02
vbias 2 1 1.6
rg 2 3 10k
m1 4 3 0 6 nmod l=3u w=30u ad=60p as=60p pd=34u ps=34u
rd 5 4 10k
cl 4 0 0.2p
vbb 6 0 -1
.model nmod nmos level=2 vto=0.8 kp=40u gamma=0 phi=0.65 nsub=2e15 xj=0.4u
+ delta=0.5 tox=40n cj=0.3m mj=0.45 cjsw=0.5n mjsw=0.33 pb=0.8
+ cgso=0.2n cgdo=0.2n cgbo=0.1n is=1e-15 rd=20 rs=20
.disto dec 10 1e3 1e10 0.9
.end

MOS3 CMOS inverter: Meyer caps and bulk junctions in .op/.ac/.tran

corpus/regress/mos3_inv.cir.ac.op.tran#
mos3_inv.cir
MOS3 CMOS inverter: Meyer caps and bulk junctions in .op/.ac/.tran
* Coverage: a level-3 inverter chain switching rail to rail (x1 drives
* x2 through every region, so DEVqmeyer's gate charges and the CJ/CJSW
* bottom and sidewall junction charges integrate across the full
* swing) and a self-biased level-3 amplifier (rf feedback, source
* degeneration with the bulk at ground, so gmbs and the reverse-biased
* source junction show in .ac) against ngspice-47. Every switching
* node carries at least 50 fF so no near-floating node crosses vds=0
* on a pulse edge.
vdd 1 0 dc 3.3
vin 2 0 dc 0 pulse(0 3.3 2n 1n 1n 8n 20n)
mn1 3 2 0 0 n3 l=1u w=4u ad=8p as=8p pd=12u ps=12u
mp1 3 2 1 1 p3 l=1u w=10u ad=20p as=20p pd=24u ps=24u
c3 3 0 50f
mn2 4 3 0 0 n3 l=1u w=4u ad=8p as=8p pd=12u ps=12u
mp2 4 3 1 1 p3 l=1u w=10u ad=20p as=20p pd=24u ps=24u
c4 4 0 100f
vac 5 0 dc 0 ac 1
cin 5 6 10p
rf 7 6 200k
mn3 7 6 8 0 n3 l=2u w=20u ad=40p as=40p pd=44u ps=44u
rs3 8 0 500
rl 1 7 10k
c7 7 0 0.2p
.model n3 nmos level=3 vto=0.6 nsub=4e16 tox=1.5e-8 xj=0.15u ld=0.05u u0=450
+ theta=0.06 eta=0.2 delta=0.6 vmax=1.6e5 kappa=0.4 nfs=6e11 rsh=15
+ cj=4e-4 mj=0.45 cjsw=3e-10 mjsw=0.3 cgso=2e-10 cgdo=2e-10 cgbo=1e-10
.model p3 pmos level=3 vto=-0.7 nsub=3e16 tox=1.5e-8 xj=0.2u ld=0.06u u0=180
+ theta=0.05 eta=0.15 delta=0.5 kappa=0.6 nfs=4e11 rsh=25
+ cj=5e-4 mj=0.5 cjsw=3.5e-10 mjsw=0.33 cgso=2.5e-10 cgdo=2.5e-10 cgbo=1e-10
.ac dec 10 10k 10g
.op
.tran 0.1n 40n
.end

corpus/regress/mos3_iv.cir.dc#
mos3_iv.cir
MOS3 I-V: level-3 NMOS/PMOS output and transfer families
* Coverage: no corpus deck has a level-3 card. This pins moseq3
* (mos3load.c) against ngspice-47: the ETA static feedback, the XJ
* short-channel factor, the DELTA narrow-width term (W=2u), THETA
* mobility degradation, VMAX velocity saturation with the KAPPA
* lateral-field channel-length modulation (n3), the plain depletion
* CLM of line510 without VMAX (p3), and the NFS weak-inversion
* exponential (the vgs grid starts in subthreshold). RD/RS come from
* RSH*NRD/NRS (prime nodes). Each device has its own E-source drive
* so every drain current is a separate branch vector; m3 runs hot
* (TEMP=80, no NFS: the hard cutoff at von) to pin MOS3temp.
vds 1 0 dc 3
vgs 2 0 dc 1
e1 11 0 1 0 1
e2 12 0 2 0 1
m1 11 12 0 0 n3 l=2u w=2u nrd=2 nrs=2
e3 21 0 1 0 -1
e4 22 0 2 0 -1
m2 21 22 0 0 p3 l=3u w=6u nrd=1 nrs=1
e5 31 0 1 0 1
m3 31 2 0 0 n3h l=4u w=10u temp=80
vbb 4 0 dc -1
e6 41 0 1 0 1
m4 41 2 0 4 n3 l=2u w=2u nrd=2 nrs=2
.model n3 nmos level=3 vto=0.7 nsub=3e16 tox=2e-8 xj=0.2u ld=0.05u u0=500
+ theta=0.08 eta=0.3 delta=1.2 vmax=1.5e5 kappa=0.5 nfs=8e11 rsh=20
.model p3 pmos level=3 vto=-0.8 gamma=0.6 nsub=2e16 tox=2e-8 xj=0.25u ld=0.08u
+ u0=200 theta=0.05 eta=0.2 delta=0.8 kappa=0.8 nfs=5e11 rsh=30
.model n3h nmos level=3 vto=0.6 kp=6e-5 phi=0.7 nsub=1e16 tox=2.5e-8 theta=0.1
+ vmax=2e5 kappa=0.3 tnom=40
.dc vgs 0 4 0.1 vds 0 5 1
.end

mos3disto.cir
MOS3 PMOS common-source stage: intermodulation in .disto
* Coverage: mos3dset.c's Dderivs chain through the semi-empirical
* current - short-channel factor (XJ, the depletion-width polynomial),
* narrow width (DELTA), static feedback (ETA), mobility modulation
* (THETA, including the C's Beta-before-TimesDeriv order that leaves
* an extra fgate in every coefficient) and channel-length modulation
* (KAPPA) - on a PMOS, through f1+f2, f1-f2 and 2f1-f2.
vdd 5 0 -5
vin 1 0 0 distof1 0.02 distof2 0.02
vbias 2 1 -1.6
rg 2 3 10k
m1 4 3 0 6 nmod l=2u w=20u ad=40p as=40p pd=24u ps=24u
rd 5 4 10k
cl 4 0 0.2p
vbb 6 0 1
.model nmod pmos level=3 vto=-0.8 kp=50u gamma=0.5 phi=0.65 nsub=1e16 xj=0.3u
+ theta=0.05 eta=0.5 kappa=0.4 delta=0.3 tox=20n cj=0.3m mj=0.45 cjsw=0.5n mjsw=0.33 pb=0.8
+ cgso=0.2n cgdo=0.2n cgbo=0.1n is=1e-15 rd=20 rs=20
.disto dec 10 1e3 1e10 0.9
.end

MOSFET noise: levels 1, 2 and 3 in a capacitively coupled cascade

corpus/regress/mosnoise.cir.noise#
mosnoise.cir
MOSFET noise: levels 1, 2 and 3 in a capacitively coupled cascade
* Coverage: mos1noi.c/mos2noi.c/mos3noi.c in their ngspice-47 form at
* the default NLEV=2 - RD/RS thermal (here from RSH*NRD/NRS, so the
* #drain/#source prime nodes exist), channel thermal 4kT*(2/3)|gm| and
* the flicker density KF*gm^2/(f^AF*W*Leff*Cox) (the 3f5 used
* KF*|Id|^AF/(f*W*Leff*Cox^2)). nm1 has no TOX, so its flicker term
* falls back to Cox for tox=1e-7 as in mos1noi.c. Each stage is biased
* by its own gate source through 1meg, whose thermal noise also shows.
vdd 1 0 dc 5
vin 2 0 dc 1.5 ac 1
m1 3 2 0 0 nm1 l=2u w=20u nrd=2 nrs=1
rl1 1 3 10k
c12 3 6 1u
rg2 6 7 1meg
vb2 7 0 dc 1.2
m2 4 6 0 0 nm2 l=3u w=30u nrd=1.5 nrs=1.5
rl2 1 4 10k
c23 4 8 1u
rg3 8 9 1meg
vb3 9 0 dc 1.1
m3 5 8 0 0 nm3 l=2u w=10u nrd=1 nrs=2
rl3 1 5 20k
.model nm1 nmos level=1 vto=0.8 kp=50u lambda=0.02 rsh=20 ld=0.2u
+ kf=1e-26 af=1.2
.model nm2 nmos level=2 vto=0.7 tox=40n nsub=1e16 uo=600 lambda=0.02
+ rsh=15 ld=0.1u kf=2e-26 af=1
.model nm3 nmos level=3 vto=0.7 tox=30n nsub=1e16 uo=500 theta=0.1
+ rsh=10 rd=5 ld=0.1u kf=5e-27 af=0.8
.noise v(5) vin dec 10 10 100meg 1
.end

off bjt behind an unscaled pulse source - NEWCONV trap regression

corpus/regress/offbjt.cir.tran#
offbjt.cir
off bjt behind an unscaled pulse source - NEWCONV trap regression
* An `off` BJT whose base is driven by a transient-function source
* (source stepping cannot scale it to zero) used to pin the device
* at zero bias in INITFIX forever: with gmin inside gbe/gbc the
* BJTconvTest current never settled (gmu = gmin/BR) and every CKTop
* strategy looped. Fixed by the ngspice junction form (gmin on the
* leakage branches), dynamic gmin stepping, and the ngspice TRANOP
* source scaling that lets source stepping zero this pulse.
vin b 0 pulse(-1.6 -1.2 10ns 400ns 400ns 100ns 10000ns)
vc c 0 2
re e 0 260
q1 c b e qstd off
.model qstd npn(is=1.0e-16 bf=50 br=0.1 rb=50 rc=10 va=50)
.tran 50ns 1us
.end

AC sensitivity: RLC ladder with coupled inductors and controlled sources

corpus/regress/sens_ac.cir.sens#
sens_ac.cir
AC sensitivity: RLC ladder with coupled inductors and controlled sources
* Coverage: no corpus deck has a .sens card. This pins sens_sens
* (ckt/cktsens.c, AC form) against ngspice-47: at each frequency the
* complex AC system is solved, then each parameter's DEVacLoad stamps
* are differenced and Y^-1 (dI - dY E) / delta is solved against the
* factored complex matrix. The filters keep every R/C/L/V/I/E/F/G/H
* vector, so the deck pins ngspice-47's AC walk of those tables
* (acmag/acphase, the AC-only capacitance and inductance, r_ac), and
* drop only the coupling kab: ngspice-47's AC sensitivity of a K
* coefficient is wrong (3.6e7 here, against -0.256+0.120j from a
* finite difference of two ngspice .ac runs, which Dune matches;
* corpus/KNOWN_DIFFS.md). One frequency on purpose: from the second
* frequency on, ngspice-47 also gets the VCCS/CCCS gains wrong (it
* redoes CKTsetup per frequency; see sens_acsweep.cir), and a
* nonlinear device would enter with gd = capd = 0 for the same reason.
vin 1 0 dc 1 ac 1 30
r1 1 2 1k
l1 2 3 10m
c1 3 0 100n
l2 4 0 5m
kab l1 l2 0.6
r4 4 0 200
i1 0 3 dc 0 ac 0.5m
e1 5 0 3 0 2
r5 5 6 1k
c2 6 0 47n
g1 0 6 4 0 1m
vs 6 7 0
r7 7 0 500
f1 0 8 vs 3
r8 8 9 1k
h1 9 0 vs 100
.sens v(8) r* c* l* v* ?1* ac lin 1 2k 2k
.end

AC sensitivity sweep: RLC ladder and voltage-output controlled sources

corpus/regress/sens_acsweep.cir.sens#
sens_acsweep.cir
AC sensitivity sweep: RLC ladder and voltage-output controlled sources
* Coverage: the frequency stepping of sens_sens (ckt/cktsens.c) against
* ngspice-47. count_steps gives LIN its point count, but inc_freq tests
* the step type against LINEAR (3) instead of SENS_LINEAR (15), so a
* linear sweep multiplies by its step too: 100, 1e4, 1e6 Hz here
* (kept by Dune). Only devices whose AC sensitivity ngspice-47 keeps
* right past the first frequency are present (R, C, L, V, I, E, H):

DC sensitivity: divider, diodes and every controlled source

corpus/regress/sens_dc.cir.sens#
sens_dc.cir
DC sensitivity: divider, diodes and every controlled source
* Coverage: no corpus deck has a .sens card. This pins sens_sens
* (ckt/cktsens.c, DC form) against ngspice-47: each parameter is
* moved by 1e-6 of its value (1e-6 when zero), the one device is
* reloaded into an empty matrix, and Y^-1 (dI - dY E) / delta gives
* the output's sensitivity. dx1 has area 2, dx2 a series RS (internal
* node; dx2:rs still comes out zero in both, since the series
* conductance is set in DIOsetup, which the walk runs before the
* perturbation) and dx3 runs at TEMP=60, so its EG sensitivity is
* live. dx4 shares dx1's model: dx1:is and dx4:is are separate
* vectors (sgen_next moves the model parameter but reloads only the
* one instance); it also keeps ngspice's unused-model pruning from
* dropping dmoda, which takes the numeric area "2.0" for dx1's model
* name otherwise. v1 is both the input and the current sense of the
* F/H pair.
* The filters (ngspice's extension of the card) keep the diodes to
* the parameters the 3f5 model has: ngspice-47 also perturbs its own
* extensions (isr, jtun, ikf, ...), several of which only switch on
* once "given", so their values are artifacts of the perturbation
* (corpus/KNOWN_DIFFS.md). At most six filters: dot_sens grows its
* filter array once, to 7 slots, and writes past it after that
* (ngspice-47 heap overflow; 8+ filters gave garbage output here).
v1 1 0 dc 5
r1 1 2 1k
r2 2 0 2k
dx1 2 3 dmoda 2.0
r3 3 0 4.7k
dx2 3 0 dmodb
i1 0 3 dc 0.2m
dx3 2 9 dmodc temp=60
r9 9 0 10k
dx4 9 0 dmoda
e1 4 0 2 0 0.5
r4 4 5 1k
g1 0 5 3 0 0.2m
r5 5 0 2.2k
f1 0 7 v1 2
r7 7 8 1k
h1 8 0 v1 300
r8 7 5 3.3k
.model dmoda d is=2e-14 n=1.2
.model dmodb d is=5e-15 rs=10
.model dmodc d is=1e-14 n=1.05 eg=1.15 xti=2.5
.sens v(7) r* ?1* dx?:is dx?:? dx?:eg dx?_*
.end

Switch hysteresis: S cards swept through VT+-VH both ways in .tran/.dc

corpus/regress/sw_hyst.cir.ac.dc.tran#
sw_hyst.cir
Switch hysteresis: S cards swept through VT+-VH both ways in .tran/.dc
* Coverage: no corpus deck has an S card. A slow triangle (0 -> 5 -> 0 V)
* drives s1 through its whole window (VT=2.4, VH=0.9: closes above 3.3,
* opens below 1.5) into a 1k load, in .tran and in a .dc. s6/s7 watch the
* mirror 5-v(1), so the one rising .dc also falls through their windows
* (ngspice runs two .dc cards in reverse deck order, Dune in deck order,
* so a second, falling .dc cannot be paired). s2/s3 share a model whose
* window (-0.6..5.4) contains the whole control range, so they keep the
* ON/OFF hint of the operating point all the way through (s2 on, s3 off). s4 has the default RON (1 ohm) and
* ROFF (1/GMIN); s5 has a negative VH, ngspice's inverted-window state
* machine (the 3f5 took |VH|). The 40u step lets swtrunc.c (ngspice)
* shorten the steps that approach each threshold. The .ac pins
* ngspice's INITSMSIG, which reads the switch state from state1: zero
* after a bare operating point, so s2 is open in AC although the
* operating point has it closed.
vc 1 0 dc 0 pwl(0 0 1m 5 2m 0)
rc 1 0 1k
vdd 2 0 dc 10 ac 1
s1 2 3 1 0 shys
rl1 3 0 1k
s2 2 4 1 0 swin on
rl2 4 0 1k
s3 2 5 1 0 swin off
rl3 5 0 1k
s4 2 6 1 0 sdef
rl4 6 0 1k
s5 2 7 1 0 sneg
rl5 7 0 1k
vo 9 0 dc 5
e1 8 9 1 0 -1
s6 2 10 8 0 shys
rl6 10 0 1k
s7 2 11 8 0 sneg
rl7 11 0 1k
.model shys sw vt=2.4 vh=0.9 ron=10 roff=1e6
.model swin sw vt=2.4 vh=3 ron=100 roff=1e5
.model sdef sw vt=2.4 vh=0.9
.model sneg sw vt=2.4 vh=-0.7 ron=50 roff=2e5
.ac lin 1 1k 1k
.dc vc 0 5 0.2
.tran 40u 2m
.end

Transfer function: BJT stage with controlled-source feedback

corpus/regress/tf_amp.cir.tf#
tf_amp.cir
Transfer function: BJT stage with controlled-source feedback
* Coverage: no corpus deck has a .tf card. This pins TFanal
* (ckt/tfanal.c) against ngspice-47: one extra solve of the factored
* operating-point Jacobian with a unit excitation on the input
* source's branch gives the gain and the input resistance; a unit
* current into the output node gives the output resistance. A
* common-emitter BJT (biased off the operating point, so the
* Jacobian holds its small-signal gm/gpi/go) drives a VCVS buffer,
* a VCCS feeds part of the output back to the base, and an F/H pair
* adds a current-controlled path, so gain, Rin and Rout are all
* nontrivial. The output is a node pair, so the third vector is
* named output_impedance_at_V(out,ref).
vin 1 0 dc 0.75
rs 1 2 2k
vcc 9 0 dc 10
rb 9 2 200k
rc 9 3 4.7k
q1 3 2 4 qn
re 4 0 330
vsense 4 5 0
r5 5 0 1meg
e1 6 0 3 0 0.5
ro 6 7 1k
rl 7 0 10k
g1 2 0 7 0 -2e-6
f1 7 0 vsense 0.1
h1 8 0 vsense 50
rref 8 0 1k
.model qn npn is=1e-15 bf=120 br=2 vaf=60 rb=50 re=2 rc=20
.tf v(7,8) vin
.end

TRA ideal line: open and shorted stubs in .ac, DC form in .op

corpus/regress/tra_ac.cir.ac.op#
tra_ac.cir
TRA ideal line: open and shorted stubs in .ac, DC form in .op
* Coverage: TRAacLoad and the MODEDC stamps of TRAload. A 50-ohm line
* (TD=1ns) carries the source to a 50-ohm load; an open stub t2
* (quarter wave at 250MHz: TD=1ns) hangs at its far end, a shorted
* stub t3 (Z0=100, NL=0.25 at F=125MHz -> TD=2ns) at the source end,
* so the sweep shows the notches and resonances of both. The sweep
* spans whole decades: ngspice-47 stretches a DEC step so the last
* point lands on FSTOP, the 3f5 does not. In .op the
* line is the 3f5 DC form: v1 = v2, i1 = -i2 (up to the (1-GMIN)
* factor), so the DC divider reads through the lines and the shorted
* stub t3 carries a real DC current into rsh; rb closes t2's far end.
vin 1 0 dc 1 ac 1
rs 1 2 50
t1 2 0 3 0 z0=50 td=1ns
rl 3 0 50
t2 3 0 4 0 z0=50 td=1ns
t3 2 0 5 0 z0=100 f=125meg nl=0.25
rsh 5 0 1
rb 4 0 1k
.ac dec 50 10meg 1g
.op
.end

TRA ideal line: matched delay, mismatched reflections, F/NL delay form

corpus/regress/tra_pulse.cir.tran#
tra_pulse.cir
TRA ideal line: matched delay, mismatched reflections, F/NL delay form
* Coverage: no corpus deck has a T card. Line t1 (Z0=50, TD=10ns) is
* driven through 50 ohms and terminated in 50 ohms: the edge reappears
* at node 3 one delay later, at half amplitude. t2 (Z0=75) feeds t3
* (Z0=50, TD from F/NL: 0.5/100MEG = 5ns) into 200 ohms || 2pF, so the
* 75/50 and 50/200 junctions bounce the wave back and forth (the
* capacitor gives the LTE control something to cut steps on). The
* triangles on v2 reverse their slope (a PULSE with PW=0 would take
* PW=TSTOP instead), which is what plants TRAaccept's delayed
* breakpoints and arms TRAtrunc.
v1 1 0 pulse(0 2 1ns 1ns 1ns 15ns 60ns)
rs1 1 2 50
t1 2 0 3 0 z0=50 td=10ns
rl1 3 0 50
v2 4 0 pwl(0 0 2ns 0 5ns 1 8ns 0 30ns 0 33ns -0.5 36ns 0)
rs2 4 5 50
t2 5 0 6 0 z0=75 td=3ns
t3 6 0 7 0 z0=50 f=100meg nl=0.5
rl3 7 0 200
cl3 7 0 2p
.tran 0.1ns 80ns
.end

TRA ideal line: charged lines discharging under UIC

corpus/regress/tra_uic.cir.tran#
tra_uic.cir
TRA ideal line: charged lines discharging under UIC
* Coverage: the MODEUIC branch of TRAload's MODEINITTRAN seed, which
* takes the line's own IC= values instead of the operating point.
* t1 starts charged to 1 V at both ends with no current (IC=V1,I1,V2,I2)
* and discharges into a matched 50 ohms at port 1: a 0.5 V step that
* lasts 2*TD, the textbook charged-line pulse generator. t2 uses the
* keyword forms (ZO=, V1=, I2=): it starts at 0.5 V on port 1 with 2 mA
* entering port 2, between mismatched 25 and 150 ohm ends, so the
* reflections ring down over several round trips.
r1 1 0 50
t1 1 0 2 0 z0=50 td=5ns ic=1,0,1,0
r2 2 0 1meg
r3 3 0 25
t2 3 0 4 0 zo=75 td=2ns v1=0.5 i2=2ma
r4 4 0 150
.tran 0.1ns 40ns uic
.end

corpus/regress/uic_getic.cir.tran#
uic_getic.cir
uic: .ic biases the semiconductors through their getic (bjtgetic.c ...)
* regression (issue #20): under UIC the 3f5 copies the .ic node
* values into every BJT/diode/MOS/JFET initial condition not given on
* the card (DEVsetic); Dune ported only CAPgetic, so these devices
* started from zero junction voltages and their charges kicked the
* first steps. q2 keeps its own IC= VBE (VCE still from the nodes);
* the diode's IC= is overwritten by its nodes in both C codes (the
* DIO_IC case never sets DIOinitCondGiven).
vcc 9 0 5
rc 9 2 2k
rb 9 1 200k
cb 1 0 10p
q1 2 1 0 qn
rc2 9 4 2k
q2 4 1 0 qn ic=0.6
d1 5 0 dd ic=0.2
rd 9 5 10k
cd 5 0 20p
m1 6 7 0 0 nm l=2u w=20u
rm 9 6 5k
rg 9 7 100k
cg 7 0 5p
.model qn npn bf=100 cje=2p cjc=1p tf=0.3n is=1e-15 rb=50
.model dd d is=1e-14 cjo=5p tt=1n
.model nm nmos level=1 vto=0.8 kp=50u cgso=1n cgdo=1n cbd=50f cbs=50f
.ic v(1)=0.72 v(2)=2.5 v(4)=1.5 v(5)=0.65 v(6)=3 v(7)=2
.tran 0.2n 40n uic
.end

BJTdriver -- 24inch lossy line -- DiodeCircuit

corpus/spice3f5/examples/ltra_1.cir.tran#
ltra_1.cir
   BJTdriver -- 24inch lossy line -- DiodeCircuit

* This unclassified circuit is from Raytheon, courtesy Gerry Marino.
* It consists of a BJT driver connected by a 24 inch lossy line to a
* passive load consisting mostly of diodes. Each inch 
* of the lossy line is modelled by 10 LRC lumps in the Raytheon
* model.

* The line parameters (derived from the Raytheon input file) are:
* L = 9.13nH per inch
* C = 3.65pF per inch
* R = 0.2 ohms per inch

* the circuit
*tran 0.1ns 60ns 0 0.5ns

v1 1 0 0v pulse(0 4 1ns 1ns 1ns 20ns 40ns)
*v1 1 0 4v pulse(4 0 1ns 1ns 1ns 20ns 40ns)
vcc 10 0 5v
*rseries 1 2 5
x1 1 2 10 bjtdrvr
*t1 2 0 3 0 z0=50.0136 td=4.38119ns rel=10
o2 2 0 3 0 lline
*x2 2 3 oneinch
*x2 100 101 twentyfourinch
*x2 100 101 xtwentyfourinch
vtest1 2 100 0
vtest2 101 3 0
x3 3 4 10 dioload
*rl 3 0 5
*dl 0 3 diod2

.model lline ltra rel=1 r=0.2 g=0 l=9.13e-9 c=3.65e-12 len=24 steplimit compactrel=1.0e-3 compactabs=1.0e-14

.model qmodn npn(bf=100 rb=100 cje=0.09375pF cjc=0.28125pF is=1e-12
+pe=0.5 pc=0.5)

.model qmodpd npn(bf=100 rb=100 cje=0.08187pF cjc=0.2525pF is=1e-12
+pe=0.5 pc=0.5)
*.model qmodpdmine npn(bf=100 rb=100  cje=0.08187pF cjc=0.15pF is=1e-12
.model qmodpdmine npn(bf=100 rb=100  cje=0.08187pF cjc=0.05pF is=1e-12
+pe=0.5 pc=0.5)

.model dmod1 d(n=2.25 is=1.6399e-4 bv=10)

.model dmod2 d

.model dmod d(vj=0.3v)

*.model diod1 d(1.0 tt=0.75ns vj=0.6 rs=909 bv=10)
.model diod1 d(tt=0.75ns vj=0.6 rs=909 bv=10)

*.model diod2 d(1.0 tt=0.5ns vj=0.3 rs=100 bv=10)
.model diod2 d(tt=0.5ns vj=0.3 rs=100 bv=10)

.options itl5=0 acct
+reltol=1e-3 abstol=1e-14
.tran 0.1ns 60ns
.save v(1) v(2) v(3)

*.tran 1e-9 1e-8

Example 3 for interconnect simulation

corpus/spice3f5/examples/ltra_2.cir.tran#
ltra_2.cir
 	Example 3 for interconnect simulation

* From neug1, Mosaic aluminum lines. 2um thick, 11um wide. Assuming
* 10um above the ground.
* Material: aluminum; resistivity (sigma) = 2.74uohm-cm = 2.74e-8 ohm-m 
* Dielectric: SiO2, dielectric constant (epsilon) =3.7 
* epsilon0 = 8.85e-12 MKS units
* mu0 = 4e-7*PI
* speed of light in free space = 1/sqrt(mu0*epsilon0) = 2.9986e8 MKS units
*
*  Line parameter calculations:
*  capacitance: parallel plate
*  C = epsilon*epsilon0 * A / l
*  C = 3.7*8.85e-12 * 11e-6 * 1(metre) / 10e-6 = 36.02e-12 F/m
*    + 30% = 46.8e-12 F/m = 0.468pF/cm
*
*  C_freespace = 46.8e-12/epsilon = 12.65e-12 F/m
*  speed of light in free space v0 = 2.9986e8 = 1/sqrt(L0*C0)
*  => L0 = 1/C0*v0^2
*  L0 = 1/(12.65e-12 * 8.9916e16) = 1/113.74e4 = 0.008792e-4 H/m
*    = 0.8792 uH/m = 8.792nH/cm
*  
*  R = sigma * l / A = 2.74e-8 * 1 / (11e-6*2e-6) = 1245.45 ohms/m
*    = 12.45ohms/cm
*
*  transmission line parameters:
*  	nominal z0 = sqrt(L/C) = 137 ohms
*	td = sqrt(LC) = 64.14e-12 secs/cm = 0.064ns/cm
*
*


vcc vcc 0 5
*v1 1 0 0v pulse(0 5 1ns 0.1ns 0.1ns 5ns 100ns)
v1 1 0 0v pulse(0 5 0.1ns 0.1ns 0.1ns 1ns 100ns)
rs 1 2 10
*xdrv 1 2 vcc bjtdrvr
*xrcv 3 4 vcc bjtdrvr
*xrcv 3 4 vcc dioload
d1 3 vcc diod
d2 0 3 diod
*cl 3 0 1pF
*o1 2 0 3 0 lline
x1 2 3 sixteencm
*x1 2 3 xonecm

.model diod d
.model lline ltra rel=1.8 r=12.45 g=0 l=8.792e-9 c=0.468e-12 len=16 steplimit

* 1cm
* 2cm
* 4cm
* 6cm
* 8cm
* 10cm
* 12cm
*.tran 0.001ns 15ns 0 0.1ns
* 24cm
.tran 0.001ns 10ns 0 0.1ns
* onecm10
*.tran 0.001ns 10ns 0 0.01ns


* 1. define the subckt r10 to be one tenth of the resistance per cm.
* 2. define the subckt onecm to be one of onecm10 (modelled using
* 10 segments), onecm8, onecm4, onecm2 and lump1. Then use
* the subckts onecm, fourcm, fivecm, tencm, twelvecm,
* twentyfourcm in the circuit. The line is modelled as rlc segments.
* 3. define the subckt xonecm to be one of xonecm10, xonecm8,
* xonecm4, xonecm2 and xlump1. Use the subckts xonecm,
* xfourcm, xfivecm, xtencm, xtwelvecm, xtwentyfourcm in the
* circuit. The line will be modelled as r-lossless lumps.

.subckt xonecm 1 2
*x1 1 2 xlump1
x1 1 2 xonecm4
.ends xonecm

.subckt onecm 1 2
*x1 1 2 lump1
x1 1 2 onecm4
.ends onecm

.subckt r10 1 2
r1 1 2 1.245
.ends r10

* ECL driver and diode receiver models - from Raytheon

.model qmodn npn(bf=100 rb=100 cje=0.09375pF cjc=0.28125pF is=1e-12
+pe=0.5 pc=0.5)

.model qmodpd npn(bf=100 rb=100 cje=0.08187pF cjc=0.2525pF is=1e-12
+pe=0.5 pc=0.5)
*.model qmodpdmine npn(bf=100 rb=100  cje=0.08187pF cjc=0.15pF is=1e-12
.model qmodpdmine npn(bf=100 rb=100  cje=0.08187pF cjc=0.05pF is=1e-12
+pe=0.5 pc=0.5)

.model dmod1 d(n=2.25 is=1.6399e-4 bv=10)

.model dmod2 d

.model dmod d(vj=0.3v)

*.model diod1 d(1.0 tt=0.75ns vj=0.6 rs=909 bv=10)
.model diod1 d(tt=0.75ns vj=0.6 rs=909 bv=10)

*.model diod2 d(1.0 tt=0.5ns vj=0.3 rs=100 bv=10)
.model diod2 d(tt=0.5ns vj=0.3 rs=100 bv=10)

* bjt driver - 19=input, 268=output, 20=vcc; wierd node numbers from 
* the Raytheon file

* Subcircuit conv2wtwentyinch
* conv2wtwentyinch is a subcircuit that models a 2-conductor transmission line with
* the following parameters: l=9.13e-09, c=3.65e-12, r=0.2, g=0,
* inductive_coeff_of_coupling k=0.482, inter-line capacitance cm=1.8e-12,
* length=20. Derived parameters are: lm=4.40066e-09, ctot=5.45e-12.
* 
* It is important to note that the model is a simplified one - the
* following assumptions are made: 1. The self-inductance l, the
* self-capacitance ctot (note: not c), the series resistance r and the
* parallel capacitance g are the same for all lines, and 2. Each line
* is coupled only to the two lines adjacent to it, with the same
* coupling parameters cm and lm. The first assumption imply that edge
* effects have to be neglected. The utility of these assumptions is
* that they make the sL+R and sC+G matrices symmetric, tridiagonal and
* Toeplitz, with useful consequences.
* 
* It may be noted that a symmetric two-conductor line will be
* accurately represented by this model.

* Lossy line models
.model mod1_conv2wtwentyinch ltra rel=1.2 nocontrol r=0.2 l=4.72933999088e-09 g=0 c=7.25000000373e-12 len=20
.model mod2_conv2wtwentyinch ltra rel=1.2 nocontrol r=0.2 l=1.35306599818e-08 g=0 c=3.65000000746e-12 len=20

The same deck with Dune's opt-in L-stable TR-BDF2 integrator (D-0027, #6) appended: the trapezoidal ring that seeds the failure is damped and the run completes. Below is what it computes — closer to a fine-step reference than the faithful mode or ngspice's own golden on this deck. Not the 3f5 contract: the oracle comparison runs plain trap, so the expected failure above stays.

Known-marginal vs the oracle XFAIL · Transient Analysis

Meyer charge is step-path dependent and the step controller is bistable here: ngspice rides a 0.1-1ns LTE limit cycle for 2us while Dune cruises at TMAX; ngspice's own 0.5ns rerun differs from its default-step golden by 0.87x the allowance, and Dune at 0.5ns matches that rerun to 8mV (op/DC/AC match at 1e-5) - D-0011

corpus/regress/bsim3_cap.cir.ac.tran#
bsim3_cap.cir
BSIM3v3.3 capMod 0/1/2 and XPART partitions in .tran/.ac, pass-gate reverse mode
* Coverage: three NMOS pass gates (capmod=0 xpart=0 i.e. 40/60,
* capmod=1 xpart=0.5 i.e. 50/50, capmod=2 xpart=1 i.e. 0/100) with
* CGSL/CGDL/CKAPPA overlap models, each charging a 100 fF load from a
* pulsed source and discharging it again, so vds changes sign every
* half period (inverse-mode charge swap) while the gate stays high;
* plus a pmos pass gate on capmod=2 with the default 40/60. The .ac
* sweep sees the same capacitance matrices at the operating point.

BSIM3v3.3 CMOS inverter chain and amplifier: capMod 3 charges in .op/.ac/.tran

corpus/regress/bsim3_inv.cir.ac.op.tran#
bsim3_inv.cir
BSIM3v3.3 CMOS inverter chain and amplifier: capMod 3 charges in .op/.ac/.tran
* Coverage: two inverters from the Berkeley 0.35um BSIM3v3.3.0 cards
* (ngspice-47 examples/mos) switching rail to rail, so the default
* charge-thickness capMod 3 gate charges, the bias-dependent capMod
* overlap charges (CGSL/CGDL default 0 -> constant CGSO/CGDO from
* XJ), and the bottom/sidewall/gate-edge junction charges integrate
* across the whole swing in both drain-source orientations; plus a
* self-biased NMOS amplifier (rf feedback, source degeneration,
* bulk at ground) for gm/gds/gmbs and the Meyer-free capacitance
* matrix in .ac. Every switching node carries >= 50 fF so no
* near-floating node crosses vds=0 on a pulse edge.
vdd 1 0 dc 3.3
vin 2 0 dc 0 pulse(0 3.3 2n 0.5n 0.5n 8n 20n)
mn1 3 2 0 0 n1 l=0.35u w=2u ad=2p as=2p pd=6u ps=6u
mp1 3 2 1 1 p1 l=0.35u w=5u ad=5p as=5p pd=12u ps=12u
c3 3 0 50f
mn2 4 3 0 0 n1 l=0.35u w=2u ad=2p as=2p pd=6u ps=6u
mp2 4 3 1 1 p1 l=0.35u w=5u ad=5p as=5p pd=12u ps=12u
c4 4 0 100f
vac 5 0 dc 0 ac 1
cin 5 6 10p
rf 7 6 200k
mn3 7 6 8 0 n1 l=1u w=20u ad=20p as=20p pd=44u ps=44u
rs3 8 0 200
rl 1 7 5k
c7 7 0 0.2p
.ac dec 10 10k 10g
.op
.tran 0.05n 40n

bsim3_iv.cir
BSIM3v3.3 output families: NMOS and PMOS 0.35um (Berkeley cards)
* Coverage: drain sweep 0..3.3 V at five gate biases for an NMOS and
* a PMOS (mirrored through E sources, so one two-source .dc drives
* both) from the Berkeley BSIM3v3.3.0 model cards shipped with
* ngspice-47 (examples/mos/modelcard.{nmos,pmos}): linear,

BSIM3v3.3 noise: common-source stage with SPICE2 and BSIM3 noise models

corpus/regress/bsim3_noise.cir.noise#
bsim3_noise.cir
BSIM3v3.3 noise: common-source stage with SPICE2 and BSIM3 noise models
* Coverage: .noise of a self-biased common-source stage from the
* Berkeley 0.35um cards: the NMOS uses noimod=1 (default; SPICE2
* channel thermal 4kT*2/3*|gm+gds+gmbs| and KF*|Id|^AF/(f^EF*Leff^2*Cox)
* flicker) with RSH/NRD/NRS for the series-resistance generators; the
* PMOS current-source load uses noimod=2 (BSIM3 Qinv thermal noise and
* the NOIA/NOIB/NOIC strong-inversion flicker of b3noi.c) with
* capMod 2 so Qinv comes from the capMod 2 inversion charge.

vac 5 0 dc 0 ac 1
cin 5 6 10p
rf 7 6 500k
mn 7 6 0 0 nn l=1u w=10u ad=10p as=10p pd=22u ps=22u nrd=1 nrs=1
vbp 9 0 dc 2.2

* Coverage: .pz of a resistively loaded common-source stage on the
* Berkeley 0.35um NMOS card (capMod 3 intrinsic capacitance matrix,
* CGSO/CGDO/CGBO overlaps, bulk junctions) driven from a source

BSIM3v3.3 transfer families at 85 C: subthreshold, body effect, DELVTO/MULU0

corpus/regress/bsim3_vg.cir.dc#
bsim3_vg.cir
BSIM3v3.3 transfer families at 85 C: subthreshold, body effect, DELVTO/MULU0
* Coverage: gate sweep 0..1.6 V in 20 mV steps (deep subthreshold
* through strong inversion, so all three Vgsteff branches and the
* n/Cdsc/Cit swing) at three body biases (Vbseff smoothing, K1/K2,
* DVT/DVT2W short-channel terms, K3/K3B narrow width) for the
* Berkeley 0.35um NMOS and PMOS (mirrored through E sources), with
* .options temp=85 against TNOM=27 so UTE/KT1/KT2/UA1/UB1/UC1/AT/PRT
* and the junction temperature laws all act; a third NMOS carries
* DELVTO and MULU0, a fourth a binned card (LVTH0/WU0/PK1-style L/W
* terms, BINUNIT=1) at a short, narrow geometry.

vg 2 0 dc 0
vb 3 0 dc 0

m3 1 2 0 3 n1 l=0.35u w=2u ad=2p as=2p pd=6u ps=6u delvto=0.05 mulu0=0.9

S-parameters of a passive RLC two-port, ports of different Z0 (ngspice .sp)

corpus/regress/sp_2port.cir.ac.op.sp#
sp_2port.cir
S-parameters of a passive RLC two-port, ports of different Z0 (ngspice .sp)
* Coverage: two RF ports (PORTNUM) with Z0 = 50 and 75 ohm around an
* RLC T-network with a shunt resonator, dec sweep across the
* resonance. Port 1 also carries a DC value and an AC stimulus: .op
* sees the source behind its 50 ohm reference resistor (internal node
* v1#res), .ac drives through it, and .sp ignores the AC stimulus
* (MODESP) and excites the ports itself. S/Y/Z against ngspice-47.
* The cards follow ngspice's run order (its analysis table, not the
* deck), which Dune's card-order run must match plot by plot.
v1 in 0 dc 1 ac 1 portnum 1
v2 out 0 dc 0 portnum 2 z0 75
r1 in a 10
l1 a mid 100n
c1 mid 0 10p
l2 mid b 1u
c2 b 0 100p
r2 b 0 1k
r3 mid out 22
rl out 0 300
.ac dec 5 1meg 1g
.op
.sp dec 10 1meg 1g
.end

S-parameters of a MOS common-source stage (ngspice .sp, non-reciprocal)

corpus/regress/sp_amp.cir.sp#
sp_amp.cir
S-parameters of a MOS common-source stage (ngspice .sp, non-reciprocal)
* Coverage: an active two-port between PORTNUM sources, so S21 and
* S12 differ by the transistor's gain (S12 only through the overlap
* and junction capacitances); the ports have no DC value and sit
* behind 50 ohm. The span is not a whole number of decades: span.c
* steps by 10^(1/n) from FSTART (the 3f5 rule), unlike ngspice-47's
* .ac, which re-spaces the points onto FSTOP. MOS1 keeps the
* operating point free of the Boltzmann/charge constants, which
* differ between the 3f5 and ngspice (KNOWN_DIFFS).
vdd vdd 0 dc 5
v1 p1 0 portnum 1
v2 p2 0 portnum 2
cin p1 g 10n
rg1 vdd g 300k
rg2 g 0 100k
m1 d g s 0 nm w=50u l=2u ad=100p as=100p pd=54u ps=54u
rs s 0 200
cs s 0 1n
rd vdd d 2k
cout d p2 10n
.model nm nmos level=1 vto=0.7 kp=60u lambda=0.02 gamma=0.4 phi=0.65
+ cgso=0.3n cgdo=0.3n cbd=50f cbs=50f mj=0.5 pb=0.8 rd=10 rs=10
.sp dec 10 1meg 500meg
.end

S-parameter noise of a BJT common-emitter stage (ngspice .sp DONOISE=1)

corpus/regress/sp_noise.cir.sp#
sp_noise.cir
S-parameter noise of a BJT common-emitter stage (ngspice .sp DONOISE=1)
* Coverage: the .sp noise correlation matrix Cy (written by ngspice as
* i(Cy_i_j)) from the transistor's shot and thermal generators and the
* bias resistors' thermal noise carried to the ports through the
* adjoint solves, plus the two-port noise parameters NF, NFmin, SOpt
* and Rn at the port-1 reference. The transistor has flicker noise
* (KF=1e-12, comparable to the base shot noise at 2 MHz), which .sp
* drops (N_GAIN path of NevalSrc). Cy itself (~1e-23 A^2/Hz) sits far
* below the comparison's abstol floor, so the gate on the noise path
* is NF/NFmin/Rn/SOpt, which are ratios of Cy entries.
vcc vcc 0 dc 12
v1 p1 0 portnum 1
v2 p2 0 portnum 2 z0 75
cin p1 b 10n
rb1 vcc b 47k
rb2 b 0 10k
q1 c b e qn
re e 0 470
ce e 0 100n
rc vcc c 1k
cout c p2 10n
.model qn npn is=1e-16 bf=120 vaf=60 rb=50 rc=5 re=1 cje=1p cjc=0.5p tf=50p kf=1e-12
.sp oct 2 2meg 64meg 1
.end
